lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: name: to-spec

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: description: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the project issue tracker — no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: disable-model-invocation: true

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: This skill takes the current conversation context and codebase understanding and produces a spec (you may know this document as a PRD). Do NOT interview the user — just synthesize what you already know.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: The issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you — run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` if not.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Process

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 1. Explore the repo to understand the current state of the codebase, if you haven't already. Use the project's domain glossary vocabulary throughout the spec, and respect any ADRs in the area you're touching.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 2. Sketch out the seams at which you're going to test the feature. Existing seams should be preferred to new ones. Use the highest seam possible. If new seams are needed, propose them at the highest point you can. The fewer seams across the codebase, the better - the ideal number is one.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Check with the user that these seams match their expectations.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 3. Write the spec using the template below, then publish it to the project issue tracker. Apply the `ready-for-agent` triage label - no need for additional triage.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: <spec-template>

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Problem Statement

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: The problem that the user is facing, from the user's perspective.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Solution

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: The solution to the problem, from the user's perspective.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## User Stories

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: A LONG, numbered list of user stories. Each user story should be in the format of:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 1. As an <actor>, I want a <feature>, so that <benefit>

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: <user-story-example>

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 1. As a mobile bank customer, I want to see balance on my accounts, so that I can make better informed decisions about my spending

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: </user-story-example>

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: This list of user stories should be extremely extensive and cover all aspects of the feature.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Implementation Decisions

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: A list of implementation decisions that were made. This can include:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - The modules that will be built/modified

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - The interfaces of those modules that will be modified

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Technical clarifications from the developer

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Architectural decisions

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Schema changes

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - API contracts

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Specific interactions

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Do NOT include specific file paths or code snippets. They may end up being outdated very quickly.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Exception: if a prototype produced a snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose can (state machine, reducer, schema, type shape), inline it within the relevant decision and note briefly that it came from a prototype. Trim to the decision-rich parts — not a working demo, just the important bits.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Testing Decisions

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: A list of testing decisions that were made. Include:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - A description of what makes a good test (only test external behavior, not implementation details)

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Which modules will be tested

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Prior art for the tests (i.e. similar types of tests in the codebase)

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Out of Scope

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: A description of the things that are out of scope for this spec.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Further Notes

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Any further notes about the feature.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: </spec-template>
